nodes.label: Altruvex Design System & Brand Reference (design.md)
nodes.rationale: The token layer: single source of truth for what Altruvex looks/sounds like; every value pulled from the live codebase (apps/www), never invented. If a token disagrees with app/globals.css, the CSS wins.

nodes.label: Altruvex Brand & Positioning
nodes.rationale: Precision web engineering firm in Cairo, anti-template, founder-direct; proof model is 'this site itself is the proof' — the website demonstrates the production standard delivered to clients.

nodes.label: "X — not Y" Copy Idiom
nodes.rationale: Signature rhetorical move: state the standard, then dismiss the cheap alternative. Rule for social: every claim should be able to finish '…not ___' — if it can't name the lazy alternative it rejects, it's not on-brand.

nodes.label: Brand Blue Token (--brand #0E70F1)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a single deep confident blue, not generic-SaaS blue; darkened to 48% L so white-on-brand passes WCAG AA (4.66:1). Fill/focus color, not a text color; the wordmark never uses it.

nodes.label: Neutral Ramp (--n-0 … --n-8)
nodes.rationale: The backbone: the site is mostly black-and-white (90% of every screen greyscale); color is an event, not a surface. Pure 0%-saturation neutrals are the engineered-neutral brand look.

nodes.label: Section Color Worlds (blue / orange / green)
nodes.rationale: Sections scoped to a local accent via --local-accent so the site stays mostly-mono while each section gets a quiet identity. Blue = brand/trust, orange = action/CTA/pricing, green = proof/shipped. One world per section; all AA-audited both modes.

nodes.label: Gradient Accent Palette
nodes.rationale: Display-only headline color (bg-clip-text), never body text. Gradient must match the section's color world, not contrast it. Rarity budget: ≤2 gradient accents per page, one per social graphic — a spotlight, not a theme.

nodes.label: Semantic State Colors (success/warning/error)
nodes.rationale: Off-limits for emphasis or branding: green means 'succeeded', not 'nice'. Approving color comes from the green world, never --success.

nodes.label: Type Scale & Font System (Outfit/Inter/Geist Mono/Vazirmatn)
nodes.rationale: Four typefaces with strict jobs. Two adjudicated deviations from the law layer: body leading 1.75 EN / 1.9 AR (above T5's band — airy premium voice on short marketing paragraphs) and display leading 1.0–1.08 (Latin display convention; Arabic headings never inherit it). Arabic letter-spacing forced to 0.

nodes.label: Eyebrow (Monospace Kicker)
nodes.rationale: Mono, uppercase, wide-tracked kicker reads as 'engineering / spec sheet' — the cheapest way to make an asset instantly look like Altruvex. Arabic drops the uppercase transform and tracking.

nodes.label: Emphasis System (Highlight / Accent / Strong / Dim)
nodes.rationale: The brand's typographic signature. Decision rule: calm/precision/quality/risk → Highlight (serif-italic); bold/value/conversion → Accent (gradient); loss-framed phrases stay Highlight even if conversion-y — coloring a warning is tonally wrong. ≤1 emphasis idea per paragraph; color and serif-italic are headline-only.

nodes.label: Motion System (GSAP 3 + Lenis)
nodes.rationale: Purposeful and quick — reveals, not decoration; not Framer Motion. Word-split rise+stagger headline reveal is the signature. Interaction hooks (magnetic, tilt) are desktop-fine-pointer-only flourishes gated on reduced-motion, pointer capability, and constrained devices.

nodes.label: 12px Button Radius Decision
nodes.rationale: Mid-radius voice adopted in the Apple design pass: not pill (consumer-friendly softness would undercut precision positioning), not sharp-corner brutalism (fights the refined Apple-adjacent surface language). 12px on a 40px control reads machined, not bouncy; nested elements follow inner = outer − padding.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Elevation System (4 levels)
nodes.rationale: Edges define depth first; each level is a tight contact layer whose opacity decays as elevation rises plus a soft key layer that grows with height. Four levels suffice — flat-with-a-whisper, not heavy material drop-shadows.

nodes.label: Liquid Glass Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Frosted, blurred, saturated panels for nav and overlays; degrades gracefully when the user prefers reduced transparency.

nodes.label: Underline Form Inputs
nodes.rationale: Underline, not box — a deliberate recognizable choice: a form reads as a stack of typographic lines rather than a grid of boxes. The box style reads as generic SaaS and breaks the brand.

nodes.label: Lucide Iconography
nodes.rationale: Lucide exclusively: thin-stroke, geometric, no fill, no duotone — pairs with the geometric type system and the 'engineering, not decoration' voice. Strictly functional markers, never decorative filler.

nodes.label: No-Photography Imagery Direction
nodes.rationale: The product uses no photography/illustration as a design element — type, tokens, geometric overlays, grain. A photo-led post is the fastest way to look like a generic agency, the brand's named enemy. Real screenshots of shipped work are the one legitimate imagery (proof, green world).

nodes.label: SectionHeading Composition Pattern
nodes.rationale: Canonical section header composes Eyebrow + h2 + optional emphasized clause + description. Passing accent=<gradient> renders <Accent> (value/conversion); omitting it renders <Highlight> (craft/restraint) — the §5 emphasis decision encoded in a single prop.

nodes.label: Social Media Translation Recipe
nodes.rationale: Five-part layout skeleton (eyebrow → headline → emphasis → body → wordmark footer), one color world, one emphasis per graphic. Litmus test: could a competitor swap their logo onto this post and have it still work? If yes, too generic.

nodes.label: Problem-Section Ember-on-Blue Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Tech-debt flag: problem-section inherits the blue world but applies an ember (orange) gradient on its heading — violates the gradient-must-match-the-world rule. Either intentional problem→action framing or a stray; open Phase 4/5 decision.
